preamble: In the uvular-r area of northwestern Europe, the voiced uvular fricative or approximant [ʁ] is vocalized in the syllable coda to the near-open central vowel [ɐ]. Standard German has [ʁ] in onsets but [ɐ] for word-final -er and a non-syllabic [ɐ̯] after stressed vowels (Oper [ˈoːpɐ], wir [viːɐ̯]), and Standard Danish has [ʁ] syllable-initially and [ɐ̯] syllable-finally.

examples.note: After stressed vowels coda /r/ becomes non-syllabic [ɐ̯], forming centering diphthongs, as also in Tor [toːɐ̯] 'gate'.
Unstressed word-final -er is a single syllabic [ɐ] (Oper [ˈoːpɐ] 'opera'), where the vowel and /r/ merge.

examples.from: stærkeste, coda /r/ (syllable-initial /r/ is [ʁ], as in brød [ˈpʁœ̝ðˀ])
